Smoothness and Properness of a Separable Penalty

Source: R/distrib_penalty.R
penalty_kinks.DistribPenalty.Rd

penalty_kinks() returns the kinks recorded on the object at construction, and is_proper() returns TRUE when there is no map or the map is square and nonsingular, and FALSE otherwise.

Arguments

pen

A DistribPenalty() object.

theta

A named list of the parent's free parameters. It is accepted by penalty_kinks(), whose result does not depend on it.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

penalty_kinks() returns a numeric vector, pen@kinks as it stands. is_proper() returns a single logical.

Details

The kinks do not move with theta, unlike those of SCAD and MCP: they are fixed by the value at which the location of the parent is held, and they are set when the penalty is built, by distrib_kinks() or by the argument kinks of distrib_penalty(). Of the named penalties, the lasso and the elastic net report 0 and heavy_penalty() reports numeric(0).

Properness is a test on the map. The parent is a density, so \(\exp(-\rho)\) integrates to one over the values at which the penalty is read, and under a square nonsingular map the value carries \(-\log\lvert\det D\rvert\), so that \(\exp(-\rho)\) integrates to one over \(\beta\) as well. A map whose rank is below its number of columns leaves directions of \(\beta\) on which the penalty does not depend, and along those directions the integral diverges. Under a map with more rows than columns and full column rank the integral does not equal one, and it depends on the hyperparameters through a constant that the value does not carry. The test reads the log_jacobian stored at construction, or the entries of a diagonal map, through dp_log_jacobian(), and returns TRUE exactly when that quantity is finite.

See also

penalty_kinks() and is_proper() for the generics, distrib_kinks() for the derivation of the kinks, penalty_null_basis.DistribPenalty() for the directions that an improper map leaves free, penalty_prox() for the proximal operator at a kink.

Examples

# The kink of the lasso is at zero for every lambda.
penalty_kinks(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 0
penalty_kinks(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(lambda = 20))
#> [1] 0

# A Student t prior has none.
penalty_kinks(heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))
#> numeric(0)

# The penalty is proper without a map and with a square nonsingular map. It
# is improper with a map that has more rows than columns, with a singular
# one, and with one that has fewer rows than columns.
c(none     = is_proper(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3)),
  square   = is_proper(lasso_penalty(map = matrix(c(2, 1, 0, 3), 2))),
  tall     = is_proper(lasso_penalty(map = rbind(diag(2), c(1, 1)))),
  singular = is_proper(lasso_penalty(map = matrix(1, 2, 2))),
  short    = is_proper(lasso_penalty(map = diff(diag(3), differences = 2))))
#>     none   square     tall singular    short 
#>     TRUE     TRUE    FALSE    FALSE    FALSE
